skill.name: security-audit
skill.description: Review command execution, tool permissions, secrets management, WebSocket security, and frontend risks before production deployment.
skill.summary: Perform a read-only security review and organize findings by urgency.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans describing audit checks; none executes commands or accesses secrets. SKILL.md defines a read-only review workflow and contains no prompt injection or other semantic security issue.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 10 uses Markdown backticks to format a file path in an audit checklist; it contains no Ruby or shell execution.
Line 11 formats a function name while instructing the reviewer to check for shell injection; it does not invoke the function or a command.
Line 16 formats allowed tool names as Markdown code and describes a permission review; no command execution occurs.
Line 21 formats .env and .gitignore filenames in a defensive checklist item; it does not execute shell syntax.
Line 23 formats the python-dotenv package name in Markdown and only asks the reviewer to verify its usage.
Line 26 formats a WebSocket endpoint path in an authentication checklist item; it contains no executable command.
The skill mentions python-dotenv as a subject for review but includes no import, environment lookup, or secret access.
The checklist recommends ensuring .env is ignored by version control; it neither reads the file nor exposes its contents.

content.value_statement: Production reviews can miss command injection, excessive permissions, exposed secrets, and unsafe input handling. This skill provides a structured, read-only audit across backend and frontend controls.
actual_capabilities: Reviews command execution for shell injection, dangerous patterns, and a 15-second timeout.
Checks Chat and Agent mode tool permissions for excessive access or bypass risks.
Reviews environment file handling, hardcoded API keys, and python-dotenv usage.
Checks WebSocket authentication, message validation, and user input injection risks.
Reviews markdown rendering, image upload handling, and sensitive client-side data.
Organizes results into critical issues, warnings, and recommendations.
limitations: The audit is read-only and does not modify vulnerable files.
The checklist assumes the repository contains the named backend, modes, and WebSocket endpoint.
It does not run automated scanners, tests, or vulnerability exploits.
Findings depend on the source files available during review and require developer verification.

use_cases.title: Predeployment Review
use_cases.description: Assess command execution, secrets, permissions, WebSockets, and frontend controls before a production release.

use_cases.title: Backend Risk Assessment
use_cases.description: Review terminal command handling, timeouts, tool restrictions, authentication, and input validation.

use_cases.title: Security Triage
use_cases.description: Create an urgency-based report that separates immediate issues, warnings, and recommended improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Security Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a read-only security audit of this repository and group findings into critical issues, warnings, and recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an initial repository review.

prompt_templates.title: Command and Permission Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review command execution and tool permissions. Check shell injection, dangerous commands, timeout enforcement, allowed tools, and permission bypass risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when backend commands or agent tools changed.

prompt_templates.title: Secrets and WebSocket Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit secrets management and WebSocket security. Check ignored environment files, hardcoded keys, authentication, message validation, and user input injection.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before exposing a WebSocket service.

prompt_templates.title: Full Production Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform the complete read-only audit. Cite evidence, explain impact, prioritize remediation, and include command, permission, secret, WebSocket, and frontend risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a detailed production readiness assessment.

output: Warning: Confirm that untrusted input cannot reach shell parsing in the terminal command handler.
Recommendation: Verify that every command execution path enforces the expected 15-second timeout.
Secrets: Check that environment files are ignored and no API keys are stored in source.
WebSocket: Verify authentication, validate message structure, and reject unsafe user input.
Review markdown rendering for cross-site scripting exposure.
Validate image upload size and format handling.
Confirm that client-side bundles contain no sensitive data.

best_practices: Provide the complete relevant repository so findings can cite implementation evidence.
Run the audit after changes to commands, permissions, authentication, uploads, or secret handling.
Verify each reported issue and prioritize fixes by impact before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat checklist coverage as proof that the application is secure.
Do not expose discovered API keys or environment values in the report.
Do not exploit a suspected vulnerability while gathering evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill modify source files?
faq.answer: No. It performs a read-only review and recommends fixes for approval.

faq.question: Which security areas does it review?
faq.answer: It covers command execution, tool permissions, secrets, WebSockets, frontend rendering, uploads, and client-side data.

faq.question: Does it run vulnerability scanners?
faq.answer: No. It reviews available source code using a defined checklist.

faq.question: Can it prove that an application is secure?
faq.answer: No. Its findings support review but do not replace testing, threat modeling, or professional assessment.

faq.question: How are results prioritized?
faq.answer: The report separates critical issues, warnings, and recommendations according to urgency.

faq.question: When should I run this audit?
faq.answer: Run it before production and after changes to commands, permissions, authentication, secrets, WebSockets, or frontend input handling.
